items.title: Make the pre-boot loading progress unmistakable
items.what: On the ShoeMoney pre-boot loading screen, the progress bar under “Downloading the game” is only a very thin brown hairline near the lower-middle of the screen, with no visible filled segment against the dark brown background.
items.why: This is the first product moment; if the bar looks empty or static, a mobile player can read the game as frozen before reaching the bout.
items.how: Increase the track to about 6–8 px high, add a warm gold filled segment with a minimum visible width, and include either a percentage label or a subtle animated sweep while assets load.

items.title: Remove the ambiguity between the Fight button and auto-start
items.what: On the Qualifier intro screen, the large gold “FIGHT” button sits in the lower center while a separate “STARTING IN 2/3/4” countdown appears directly beneath it.
items.why: A touch-first player cannot tell whether they should tap the button or wait for the countdown, creating hesitation at the exact moment the first interaction should feel clear.
items.how: If tapping skips the countdown, label the button “START NOW” and change the subtext to “Auto-starts in 3.” If the match always auto-starts, remove the button styling and make one combined countdown control that reads “FIGHT IN 3.”

items.title: Tighten the portrait combat framing around the fighters
items.what: On the live portrait gameplay screens, the fighters’ readable bodies occupy roughly the middle band of the screen, with a large mostly empty smoky dojo/window area above them and the touch controls starting below them.
items.why: The player needs to read hands, feet, contact distance, and hit timing on a 390 px-wide phone; the current framing gives too much vertical space to non-interactive background and makes the bout harder to parse.
items.how: Add a portrait camera preset that scales the fighters up about 10–15%, lowers the visible background crop, and keeps both fighters’ feet safely above the joystick panel.

items.title: Differentiate the left and right stance-stick labels
items.what: In the live gameplay move helper strip above the joysticks, the STANCE column labels both horizontal inputs as “step”: “◀ step” and “▶ step.”
items.why: The on-screen tutorial does not teach the difference between moving toward the opponent and moving away, so the core left-stick vocabulary is unclear during the player’s first bout.
items.how: Rename the horizontal stance labels to distinct player-relative actions such as “away” and “toward,” or “back step” and “forward step,” and mirror the wording correctly if the player side changes.

items.title: Make half-point scores legible in the top HUD
items.what: On the result/win screen, HasanAbi’s top-right HUD score shows a large red “2” with a tiny stacked “1/2” squeezed beside it, while the main result below reads more clearly as “0 – 2½.”
items.why: Half-points are core scoring information, and the cramped fraction can be missed or misread at a glance during a fast point-karate exchange.
items.how: Render fractional scores as a single consistent token, such as “2.5” or a custom “2½” glyph at the same visual height as the integer score, with fixed-width score slots so the HUD does not reflow.
